sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the north-eastern edge of Palmyra along the Riverton line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Broad Street and the P.R.R. run up the page on the right. The drawn area stretches from 4th Street at the left edge to Broad Street at the right, and from Garfield Avenue near the bottom up to Elm Avenue, which forms the borough limit running diagonally across the top. Beyond that line the sheet says to see the map of Riverton. Morgan and Maple Avenues cross the middle, with 5th Street between 4th Street and Broad. The blocks are mostly frame dwellings of two and a half storeys on deep lots with sheds and auto houses behind. Larger buildings include the Central Baptist Church (brick, with a spire) near Maple Avenue, the Epworth M. E. Church with its Sunday school at Morgan Avenue and 5th Street, a large concrete-block garage and the Y.M.C.A. of Palmyra and Riverton on the Broad Street frontage, and the Palmyra Electric Co. and an undertaker and an auto show room in the top right block. Several lots near the top left are largely open ground with chicken coops. The railroad tracks lie beyond Broad Street, which is marked as 65 feet to the P.R.R. tracks, and are not drawn. Four-inch and sixteen-inch water pipes are marked along the streets. The compass at upper left shows north pointing up and to the left. A scale bar and the Sanborn copyright line sit in the bottom margin. The sheet adjoins sheets 3 and 7 to the right and below, and sheets 6 and 14 to the left.
notes: Streets are drawn as Elm Av., Maple Av., Morgan Av., Garfield Av., 4th St., 5th St. and E. Broad; today's OpenStreetMap names for the numbered streets are East 4th Street and East 5th Street.
The top left diagonal is the borough limit between Palmyra and Riverton, labelled 'See Map of Riverton, N.J.'; Elm Avenue is printed along it.
Broad Street junctions were not used for control: no roadway lines are drawn, only the lots and the note '65 to P.R.R. tracks'.
Fitted scale is about 7.80 px/ft, about 1.5 percent below the other 50 ft sheets of the atlas.

50 ft. Maple, Morgan, Garfield Avenues between 4th Street and East Broad; Elm Avenue along the Riverton borough line at the top. Broad not used (lots drawn to the P.R.R. right of way, no roadway). 7 junctions; fitted scale 7.80 px/ft, 1.5 percent under most 50 ft sheets.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the northern residential blocks of Palmyra between Broad Street and Wallace Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Broad Street and the P.R.R. line run up the left edge while Lincoln, Washington and Highland Avenues climb diagonally to the right. Spring Garden runs down the middle across the avenues, and Wallace crosses the upper right. The borough limit, a dash-dot line labelled as the boundary of the Borough of Palmyra, cuts across the top beside the note 'See Map of Riverton, N. J.', so that the strip of blocks above Lincoln Avenue is only partly drawn. Morgan Avenue closes the sheet along the bottom, with a wedge-shaped block between it and Highland Avenue at the lower left. Nearly every building is a frame dwelling of one and a half to two and a half storeys with small outbuildings behind, a few of them tile-faced, set on regular narrow lots with house numbers in the 600s and 700s. A machine shop stands at the lower right near Highland Avenue and Spring Garden, where a row of semi-detached houses lines Spring Garden. Water pipes of four, eight and sixteen inches run in the streets. The compass at the upper left points north up and to the left. Block numbers 218 to 224 and a scale bar are printed on the sheet. The left margin refers to sheet 2 across Broad Street, the right margin to sheet 4 and the bottom to sheet 7.
notes: Spring Garden is today's Spring Garden Street, and East Spring Garden Street between Morgan and Cinnaminson Avenues.
Wallace is today's Wallace Street.
Broad Street is drawn as a 160 ft right of way with the P.R.R. tracks in it and no roadway lines, so its junctions were not used.
The Spring Garden / Morgan Avenue control point was hand-picked on the bottom row of the sheet.

50 ft. Lincoln, Washington, Highland, Morgan Avenues between Broad and Wallace, Spring Garden; borough limit with Riverton at the top. Broad (160 ft right of way with the P.R.R.) not used. Weak control: mostly along Spring Garden plus Wallace junctions (one placed beyond the right edge by boundary mode); Spring Garden / Morgan hand-picked.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the north-eastern residential blocks of Palmyra between Wallace and Charles, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the avenues rise diagonally to the right. Lincoln Avenue crosses the top, Washington Avenue and Highland Avenue the middle, and Morgan Avenue the lower right, all running across Wallace, 7th Street and Charles. Wallace bends as it runs down the left side, and 7th Street, which is wider at its upper end, runs down the right of the centre with blank ground beyond it. Charles forms the right edge of the drawn area, with the note that the ground beyond it is on sheet 16. The blocks are lined with frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys on deep narrow lots, with house numbers 800 to 849 on the north side and 700s on the left. Two houses at the top are marked hollow tile, and a few dwellings are drawn with blue brick or stucco colouring. A shop marked vacant stands at the lower left on Morgan Avenue beside Wallace. The upper right corner is blank apart from the Palmyra cartouche, the compass and a boundary line. A narrow strip at the extreme upper left is marked as the borough limits. Four, eight and sixteen inch water pipes are marked along the avenues. A scale bar and the Princeton Map Division stamp sit at the bottom. The sheet adjoins sheet 3 on the left, sheet 5 on the right, and sheet 8 below.
notes: Wallace is today's Wallace Street, and Charles is East Charles Street north of Cinnaminson Avenue.
Junctions with Wallace and Charles at the sheet edge are placed from the drawn edge plus half the street width.
50 ft. Lincoln, Washington, Highland, Morgan Avenues between Wallace and Charles, with 7th Street; Wallace and Charles junctions placed from one drawn edge.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the eastern edge of Palmyra at the Cinnaminson Township line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The streets are drawn almost square to the page: Lincoln, Washington and Highland Avenues run across, with 7th Street at the left and Park Avenue at the right, and Charles runs diagonally at the lower left. A broken line lettered as the boundary between the Borough of Palmyra and Cinnaminson Township runs down the right of centre and turns diagonally at the bottom along Cleveland Avenue, so that the area east of it is only partly drawn. A second borough limit line runs along the top under the note 'See Map of Riverton, N. J.'. The blocks between 7th Street and the township line hold rows of frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys on narrow lots numbered in the 900s, with open ground behind them. One small hollow tile dwelling is marked in the top block. Blocks 302 to 304 and 234 and 240 are numbered. East of Park Avenue, beyond the township line, only a few houses are drawn, marked with exposure notes, and a few buildings are cut off along the bottom edge. A compass stands in the open ground in the middle and a scale bar in the bottom margin. Water mains of four, six and eight inches are marked along the streets. The sheet adjoins sheet 4 on the left and sheet 16 at the bottom, which is not among the scanned images.
notes: Charles is today's East Charles Street, and 7th Street keeps its name.
Park Avenue junctions carry residuals of 3 m, which may reflect a modern Park Avenue line that differs from the drawn one.
Cleveland Avenue / Highland Avenue was left out of the fit (3.3 m residual) because the street is drawn as the diagonal boundary line.

50 ft. Lincoln, Washington, Highland Avenues between 7th Street and Park Avenue, Elm Terrace, Cleveland Avenue; drawn square to its own streets (rotation -31, the eastern grid turns about 20 degrees). Park Avenue junctions carry about 3 m; Cleveland Avenue (diagonal on the Cinnaminson Township line) left out. Ground beyond Park Avenue mostly blank.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the central business and residential blocks of Palmyra on both sides of Cinnaminson Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Broad Street runs up the right edge and the cross streets run across the page. Cinnaminson Avenue and Le Coney Avenue cross the sheet from side to side, with 4th Street at the left and 5th Street near the middle, which bends diagonally at the bottom where Horace Avenue and Delaware Avenue run up the page at an angle. Beside 4th Street a narrow Berkley Avenue is lettered at the left edge. West of 5th Street the blocks hold frame dwellings of two to three storeys on deep lots with sheds and outbuildings. East of 5th Street the Broad Street frontage is commercial: a drug store, offices, the Broadway Palace moving picture house in concrete block, a department store, a tailor, stores and flats, and a large garage of 16 car capacity, with the Palmyra Hotel in the lower right. A row of brick buildings stands along the diagonal side of block 10. A concrete block manufactory sits beside 5th Street at the lower left, and the Independent Fire Co. with its fire gong lies in the lower right corner on Delaware Avenue. A cemented-floor garage of 16 cars stands at Delaware Avenue near Broad. The tracks of the railroad are not drawn; Broad is marked as 65 feet to the railroad tracks. Block numbers 6 to 15 are shown and the compass is placed in open ground at the right. The margin numbers refer to sheets 2, 7, 9, 10, 11, 14 and 15.
notes: Le Coney is today's Leconey Avenue; 4th and 5th Streets here are West 4th Street and West 5th Street in OpenStreetMap.
Broad Street is lettered East Broad above Cinnaminson Avenue and West Broad below it.
50 ft. Cinnaminson, Le Coney, Berkley, Horace, Delaware Avenues between 4th Street and Broad; West Broad junctions usable (roadway drawn).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the centre of Palmyra on the south-east side of the Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Amboy Division), drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Broad Street runs up the left edge of the page. The railroad and its platforms occupy the middle of the wide Broad Street right of way, marked as 165 to 190 feet wide north of Cinnaminson Avenue and 115 feet south of it, with East Broad lettered north of Cinnaminson Avenue and West Broad south of it; the passenger depot and a gateman's house stand beside the tracks. The blocks between Morgan Avenue, Garfield Avenue and Parry Avenue, from the railroad to Spring Garden Street and beyond it towards the next sheet, hold the town's civic buildings: the Palmyra National Bank, the First Lutheran Church, a club, police headquarters, and a building with the post office on the ground floor and a lodge room and stage above. Christ Episcopal Church and its chapel stand on Garfield Avenue. Cinnaminson Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet diagonally; south of it lie a cemetery, Society Hall and a private road, and east of Spring Garden Street the two Palmyra Public Schools, numbers 1 and 2, with a boys' play ground and a park strip beside Parry Avenue. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings with stables, garages and coops. Highland Avenue is shown only where it meets Morgan Avenue at the top edge, and the lower right corner is left blank as part of sheet 15. Water mains of 4, 6, 8 and 16 inches are marked along the streets and across the railroad.
notes: Spring Garden between Morgan and Cinnaminson Avenues is East Spring Garden Street in OpenStreetMap; south of Cinnaminson it is Spring Garden Street.

Broad Street is drawn as one wide right of way with the railroad in the middle; today East Broad Street and West Broad Street run on either side of the tracks, so Broad junctions were not used for control.
Parry Avenue met Cinnaminson Avenue at an acute angle; the modern junction lies about 10 m along Cinnaminson Avenue from the drawn one and was not used.

Palmyra National Bank, First Lutheran Church, post office, police headquarters, Christ Episcopal Church, Society Hall, Palmyra Public Schools Nos. 1 and 2, passenger depot of the Pennsylvania Railroad.

50 ft. Pilot-area sheet: Morgan, Garfield, Parry, Cinnaminson Avenues, Spring Garden, with Broad Street as a 165 to 190 ft right of way carrying the P.R.R. in the middle (Broad junctions not used: no roadway lines drawn and modern East/West Broad run either side of the tracks). Parry / Cinnaminson (acute junction) is about 10 m from the modern node and was left out. Control is 4 junctions along Spring Garden plus the Cinnaminson Avenue rail crossing: weak, held by the second pass.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the residential blocks of eastern Palmyra between Wallace and Charles, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the avenues rise diagonally to the right. Morgan Avenue runs across the top left, Garfield Avenue and Parry Avenue cross the middle and lower part, and Columbia Avenue runs diagonally in the upper right between Morgan and Garfield, meeting Charles at the right edge. Wallace is the north to south street on the left, and Charles, running slightly off the vertical, closes the drawn area on the right, with the ground beyond it left to sheet 16. The district is almost wholly dwellings, mostly frame houses of one and a half to two and a half storeys with open first-floor porches marked, on long narrow lots with sheds and small outbuildings behind. A few dwellings are faced in brick or hollow tile, and three double houses along Garfield Avenue are drawn with concrete block party walls. Blocks 4 and 23 to 28 and 227 are numbered, and the upper left and lower left corners are largely blank or hold only the compass and a few houses. Four-inch water pipes run along the avenues and Charles. A scale bar and the Princeton Map Division stamp sit at the bottom right. The margin numbers send the reader to sheet 4 at the top, sheet 7 on the left, sheet 15 at the bottom and sheet 16 on the right.
notes: Wallace is today's Wallace Street, and Charles is East Charles Street.
Columbia Avenue / Garfield Avenue, a short distance from Wallace, was not detected.
50 ft. Morgan, Garfield, Columbia, Parry Avenues between Wallace and Charles.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the south-western residential edge of Palmyra, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Berkley Avenue runs along the top of the drawn area with a short block of lots below it between 3rd Street and 4th Street. Horace Avenue and Delaware Avenue climb diagonally from the lower left, and the long narrow lots between them are numbered in the 200s and 300s. A separate 4th Street at the upper right and another 4th Street between Horace and Delaware Avenues run down the page at an angle, and 3rd Street is drawn twice, once at the lower left where it meets Delaware Avenue and once at the lower right beside the large block 206. Front and 2nd Street enter from the bottom edge. The blocks hold frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys, mostly facing the avenues, with sheds and small outbuildings; a few are marked as brick, cement block or with a brick first floor, and one building at the lower left is marked as a shop. The Palmyra Sewerage Pumping Station, a small tile building, stands alone in open ground at the upper left near the compass. The lower right holds block 245 with a cement block dwelling, a storehouse, a lumber storage shed and a wagon shed, and the big block 206 is largely empty. Block numbers 52, 53, 244, 245 and 309 appear. The sheet adjoins sheet 14 above, sheet 6 on the right and sheet 10 below right, with sheet 15 to the right of the middle. A scale bar and the Princeton Map Division stamp sit at the bottom.
notes: Streets here do not all keep their 1925 names: the 3rd Street drawn at the lower left (meeting Delaware Avenue) is today's West 2nd Street, and the 4th Street drawn between Horace and Delaware Avenues is today's Bartlett Street.

The upper 3rd Street and upper 4th Street are today's West 3rd Street and West 4th Street; modern West 3rd Street continues south of Berkley Avenue to Horace Avenue where the 1925 sheet draws only lot lines, so Horace Avenue / West 3rd Street was excluded.
Front is today's Front Street.
Delaware Avenue / West 4th Street lies about 88 ft beyond the edge of the sheet and was not used.

50 ft. Berkley, Horace, Delaware Avenues with 3rd, 4th, 2nd and Front Streets. The 3rd St. drawn at the lower left (south of Horace) is today's West 2nd Street and the 4th St. between Horace and Delaware is today's Bartlett Street (checked on an overlay); modern West 3rd Street south of Berkley follows a line not drawn in 1925 (Horace / West 3rd excluded). Palmyra Sewerage Pumping Station.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows the south-western part of Palmyra between Horace Avenue and Race Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that W. Broad runs up the right edge. Delaware Avenue crosses the upper half diagonally from lower left to upper right, with Horace Avenue just inside the top left corner. Vine runs across the lower middle and Race along the bottom edge. The numbered streets, 3rd at the far left, 4th, 5th and 6th, run down the page, and a diagonal 6th Street leaves Delaware Avenue near the centre. The most prominent building is Palmyra Public School No. 3, a large brick structure with fireproof construction built in 1922, with an auditorium on the first floor and a gymnasium on the second, set in an open lot between 4th and 5th Streets. Block 104 at the left and block 312 beside 6th Street are largely empty ground. Elsewhere frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys, with sheds and small barns behind, line Delaware Avenue, Vine, 5th and 6th Streets, and the right side of the sheet along Broad carries a row of dwellings, shops and flats numbered in the 200s and 300s, with a pink-coloured building group at the top right. A scale bar and the Princeton Map Division stamp sit at the lower left. Water pipes of four and eight inches are marked in the streets. The margin refers to sheet 9 on the left, sheet 6 above, sheet 15 on the right and sheet 12 below.
notes: The numbered streets are West 3rd to West 6th Street in OpenStreetMap; the diagonal 6th Street leaving Delaware Avenue is West 6th Street.
Vine and Race keep their names (Vine Street, Race Street).
The 4th Street lettered beside Horace Avenue at the top left is today's Bartlett Street.
Race Street / West Broad Street was not detected; Race Street junctions on the bottom row are placed from the drawn edge.
50 ft. Horace, Delaware Avenues, Vine and Race between 3rd Street and West Broad; Public School No. 3. The 4th St. at the top left is today's Bartlett Street. Fitted scale 7.80 px/ft.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the western edge of the Palmyra built-up area, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Arch and Market Streets run across the page and Jefferson, Washington, Front, 2nd and 3rd Streets run down it. The sheet shows a grid of large blocks, numbered 204 to 206, 244 to 249 and 251 to 253, of which most hold only a scatter of dwellings and outbuildings and several are almost empty. The upper left quarter, blocks 244 and 245, is open ground with the compass and no buildings drawn. The built-up part lies around 2nd and 3rd Streets: frame dwellings of one and a half to two storeys, a few with concrete-block walls, flats and small stores, and two narrow cement-block structures in the top row on Arch Street. Two churches are lettered: the Union A.M.E. Church, heated by hot air and lit by kerosene lamps, in block 205 beside 3rd Street, and the Evergreen Baptist Church, a blue-coloured building lighted by gas and heated by stove, in block 204 at the lower right. A diagonal edge cuts across the lower right corner, beyond which the sheet is blank and marked 'No Exposure'. House numbers in the 800s and 900s run along the north to south streets and 1500s and 1600s along Arch and Market. A scale bar and the Princeton Map Division stamp sit at the bottom right. The right margin refers to sheet 12. Water pipes of four inches are marked in the streets.
notes: Washington, between Jefferson and Front, is today's Kennedy Street in OpenStreetMap.
2nd Street and 3rd Street are today's West 2nd Street and West 3rd Street; Arch and Market are Arch Street and Market Street.
The sheet's diagonal lower right edge is annotated 'No Exposure'.
50 ft. Arch and Market at Jefferson, Washington, Front, 2nd, 3rd Streets; Union A.M.E. and Evergreen Baptist Churches. Printed Washington is today's Kennedy Street. Fitted scale 7.76 px/ft.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the western residential blocks of Palmyra on the south-west side of the Pennsylvania Railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that West Broad Street and the numbered streets run up the page. The sheet spans the blocks between Race Street at the top and Market Street near the bottom, and from 3rd Street on the left edge to West Broad Street on the right, with Arch Street crossing the middle and 4th, 5th and 6th Streets running parallel to Broad. The blocks are mostly frame dwellings, many of two and a half storeys, set on long narrow lots with sheds, auto houses and a few concrete-block garages behind them. Near West Broad Street the drawing is denser: the West End Hotel stands at the corner of Race Street, a group of stores occupies the frontage near Arch Street, and the Arch Street Station of the railroad is drawn on the far side of Broad, with the tracks only indicated as lying beyond the street. South of Market Street the sheet shows parts of four further blocks, including a Sunday school building on 5th Street, cut off diagonally along the boundary of the area drawn on sheet 14; the triangle beyond is left blank. Water pipes of four and eight inches are marked along the streets, and fire hydrants at several corners. House numbers on 3rd to 6th Streets run in the 300s to 600s and on Broad in the 1400s and 1500s. The sheet adjoins sheet 10 above, sheet 11 to the left, sheets 13 and 15 across Broad and sheet 14 below.
notes: The 1925 numbered streets are today's West 3rd, West 4th, West 5th and West 6th Street in OpenStreetMap.
West End Hotel at West Broad and Race; Arch Street Station of the Pennsylvania Railroad across West Broad.

50 ft. Pilot sheet: Race, Arch, Market at 3rd to 6th Streets and West Broad. Detector ink_below_paper 80 chosen here (138: RMSE 5.6 m with two narrow pairs; 100, 80, 60: about 1 m). Race / 6th and Race / West Broad hand-picked from the pilot detection (a fresh run locked Race / 6th onto a lot line).

sheet-13-1.description: The main part of sheet 13 covers the south-western edge of Palmyra between West Broad Street and Charles Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that West Broad Street runs up the left edge. Pennsylvania Avenue runs along the top, New Jersey Avenue and Public Road cross the sheet, and Fillmore Avenue runs along the bottom; Spring Garden runs down the middle between Pennsylvania Avenue and Public Road. The two upper rows of blocks are residential, with a row of small frame dwellings on Pennsylvania Avenue and scattered houses on New Jersey Avenue and Public Road. The industrial part of the sheet lies along West Broad Street and a railroad siding that curves off the Pennsylvania Railroad: the Palmyra Foundry and Machine Company with its foundry floor, moulding shop, core room, machine shop and coke storage occupies the corner of West Broad Street and Public Road, and the remains of the burnt Bituco Manufacturing and Chemical Company stand across Public Road. At the foot of the sheet, beside a second siding at Fillmore Avenue, is the yard of H. B. Williams, dealer in ice, coal and grain, with an office, storage sheds and a coal pocket. Much of the large block between Public Road and Fillmore Avenue is empty, and Charles is drawn only as a diagonal street across the open ground in the lower right corner, with no buildings beyond it. An inset in a heavy frame at the right, described separately, shows two works farther along West Broad Street. Water mains of four inches are marked along the streets.
notes: Fillmore Avenue is spelled Filmore Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Charles is today's West Charles Street, but its drawn diagonal no longer matches the modern street near Public Road (New River Road), so it was not used for control.
Palmyra Foundry and Machine Company; remains of the Bituco Manufacturing and Chemical Company after a fire; H. B. Williams, ice, coal and grain.

50 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main map): Pennsylvania, New Jersey Avenues, Public Road, Fillmore Avenue between West Broad and Charles; Palmyra Foundry and Machine Co., H. B. Williams coal yard. Charles (diagonal) left out: the modern street (West Charles / New River Road) is realigned near Public Road. Fillmore / West Broad hand-picked. Part 2: inset in a heavy frame at the right showing West Broad Street frontage of block 212 farther south (1398 to 1400 W. Broad: Delaware River Engineering Co., Standard Enameling Mfg. Co.) with the P.R.R. siding; no street junction, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: West Broad Street frontage of block 212 south of the main map (Delaware River Engineering Co., Standard Enameling Mfg. Co.) (no street junction; position along West Broad not fixed by anything drawn; needs hand-picked control from a source locating these works (the inset shows only West Broad and the railroad)).

sheet-14-1.description: The main part of sheet 14 covers the north-western corner of Palmyra along the Delaware River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that the riverfront runs up the left side of the page. It reaches from the river bank and Bank Avenue east to 4th Street, and from Morgan Avenue, which follows the borough line with Riverton, south across Garfield Avenue and Cinnaminson Avenue to Le Coney Avenue and Berkley Avenue. Above Morgan Avenue the ground belongs to Riverton and is left blank with a note to see the map of Riverton; Front Street and Elm Avenue are drawn there only as street lines, and the borough limits are lettered along Elm Avenue. On the river bank stand the works of the Riverton and Palmyra Water Company: the main pumping station with its suction pipes, a well, and pumping stations Nos. 2 and 3 along Bank Avenue, together with boat houses and a hoist house at the water's edge. Cinnaminson Avenue continues as a road onto the river, where the ferry pier shown in the inset above begins. The large block 242 between Garfield and Cinnaminson Avenues is nearly empty apart from a gasoline station, and block 243 south of Cinnaminson Avenue has only a few buildings. East of 2nd Street the blocks are built up with frame dwellings; the Jensen Manufacturing Company's washing-machine works, with its erecting shop and machine room, lies between Morgan and Garfield Avenues, and a printing shop stands on Cinnaminson Avenue. The blocks between 3rd and 4th Streets on Le Coney Avenue are closely built with small houses. Below Berkley Avenue the ground belongs to sheet 9 and is blank. The lower left corner holds a separately drawn inset.
notes: Le Coney Avenue is Leconey Avenue in OpenStreetMap; 2nd Street north of Cinnaminson Avenue is East 2nd Street, 4th Street is East 4th Street north and West 4th Street south of Cinnaminson Avenue, 3rd Street is West 3rd Street.
East Temple Boulevard, the approach to the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge, now cuts diagonally across the blocks between 2nd and 4th Streets.
Riverton and Palmyra Water Company pumping stations; Jensen Manufacturing Company, washing machines.

100 ft. Three parts. Part 1 (main map): riverfront from Bank Avenue to 4th Street, Morgan to Berkley Avenues; Riverton and Palmyra Water Co. pumping stations, Jensen Mfg. Co. Part 2: inset at top left, the Tacony-Palmyra Ferry Co. pier at the end of Cinnaminson Avenue; placed from one point carried from part 1 plus a derived point (helmert, low confidence). Part 3: inset at lower left, Orchard and Legion Avenues between 5th Street and West Broad, drawn at another rotation (+54 degrees).

sheet-14-2.description: This inset at the top left of sheet 14 shows the pier of the Tacony-Palmyra Ferry Company, which ran out into the Delaware River from the end of Cinnaminson Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch in a frame of heavy lines above the main map. A long timber pier carries the road to the ferry from the river bank, at the right where Cinnaminson Avenue is lettered, out to the ferry slip at the left end. Along its north side stand small buildings on piles: an office, a machine shop and a store, with a lift and the slip at the outer end and a fire hydrant on the pier. A four-inch water pipe runs along the road for most of the pier's length. The river is lettered across the inset above and below the pier, and the bank at the right is drawn with a short stretch of the shore line. Nothing else is shown; the land end joins the main part of the sheet, where Cinnaminson Avenue meets the river near the water company's pumping station. The ferry was replaced in 1929 by the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge, and the pier no longer exists, so the inset could only be placed by matching its land end to the same point on the main map and assuming the main map's scale and orientation.
notes: Placed from one point carried from part 1 (the shore end of the pier on the line of Cinnaminson Avenue) and a derived point 300 ft out along the pier; scale and rotation are those of part 1. Low confidence.

sheet-14-3.description: This inset in the lower left corner of sheet 14 shows a small residential district on the north-west side of West Broad Street and the Pennsylvania Railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned at a different angle from the rest of the sheet, with its own north arrow pointing to the right. It covers Orchard Avenue and Legion Avenue, which run from West Broad Street up to and beyond 5th Street, crossed by 5th Street and 6th Street, with Market Street at the right-hand edge. The blocks are laid out in narrow numbered building lots, many still vacant; frame dwellings of one and a half to two storeys stand mostly on Orchard Avenue and along the lower part of Legion Avenue, with a few on 6th Street and in block 209. Along the bottom of the inset West Broad Street runs beside the tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Amboy Division), and a freight station stands on the far side of the line, with the ends of the blocks beyond it on Fillmore Avenue, which belong to sheet 13. A four-inch water pipe is marked along West Broad Street and 5th Street. A long straight line crossing blocks 209, 109 and 108 marks the edge of what is drawn on sheet 12, which covers the adjoining ground to the right.
notes: 5th and 6th Street are West 5th and West 6th Street in OpenStreetMap; Fillmore Avenue is Filmore Avenue.
Palmyra Bridge Boulevard (Route 73) now crosses this area.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers a large, thinly built area in the south of Palmyra between the Pennsylvania Railroad and Charles Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that West Broad Street runs up the left edge beside the railroad (Camden and Amboy Division). It reaches from Cinnaminson Avenue, which crosses the top of the sheet diagonally, down to Pennsylvania Avenue at the bottom. Most of the middle of the sheet is open ground: a large tract numbered 310 with an athletic field and grand stand, crossed only by the ends of Walnut and Spring Garden and the outlines of lots. A private road runs from Cinnaminson Avenue towards West Broad Street. The built-up parts are along the edges. On Cinnaminson Avenue and the short streets south of it, Wallace and Pear, are rows of frame dwellings, with houses also on Spring Garden north of Walnut and along Charles. A line of houses fronts West Broad Street south of the athletic field. Along Park Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue near Spring Garden stand the West Palmyra Hotel, a blacksmith's shop, rows of small dwellings and the yard of the Palmyra Concrete Company. Charles runs diagonally down the right side, with the ground beyond it marked as having no exposure and left to sheet 16, which is not among the scanned images. Water pipes of two to eight inches are marked along the streets. The sheet adjoins sheets 6, 10 and 12 across the railroad, sheets 7 and 8 above and sheet 13 below.
notes: Spring Garden north of Walnut no longer follows its 1925 line: its junction with Cinnaminson Avenue was 12 m from the modern one and was left out; Walnut, Pear and Charles have since been extended across the athletic field tract.
Charles is East and West Charles Street in OpenStreetMap.
